title: A One-Parameter, Four-Channel Consistency Test for EFC Background Coupling (β · T(a))
description: Tests a single-parameter Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) background-coupling modification of the Friedmann equation against four independent probes: BAO distances, redshift-space distortions, CMB lensing, and Type Ia supernovae. Finds that a positive background coupling (β ≈ 0.08) mildly improves BAO+RSD fits (Δχ2 = -3.89) while remaining consistent with CMB lensing and SN Ia, and that Poisson-channel modification is excluded by growth data. The transition function T(a) naturally suppresses deviations at high redshift, ensuring GR recovery at recombination and earlier.

modified_friedmann.description: EFC background-coupling architecture: a single parameter \beta rescales the dark-energy term by a fixed transition function T(a) that vanishes as \Omega_m \to 1.

distance_coupling_kernel.description: Kernel defining the standard EFC transition function; it ties coupling strength to the non-matter fraction and suppresses modifications at early times.

growth_ode.description: Linear growth equation; the EFC background modification alters H(a), increasing Hubble friction and suppressing late-time growth.

poisson_channel_alternative.description: Alternative (excluded) coupling route: \mu>1 enhances growth and is disfavoured by BOSS DR12 RSD; EFC favours background (not Poisson) coupling.

key_results.main_finding: Background coupling with a single parameter (β ≈ 0.08) passes four independent probes and yields a mild BAO+RSD preference over ΛCDM, while the Poisson-channel modification is excluded by growth data.
parameters_tested: T(a) (fixed transition function; vanishes as Ωm→1)
datasets_used: BOSS DR12 BAO distances (DM/rd, DH/rd at z = 0.38, 0.51, 0.61)

sealed_predictions.statement: High-redshift Lyα P1D (z ≈ 3) shows a null EFC background imprint (effect strongly suppressed as T(a) → small), delivering no detectable deviation from ΛCDM within current precision.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Lyα 1D flux-power measurements at z ≈ 3 detecting a robust (>3σ) deviation attributable to background-only coupling.

sealed_predictions.statement: Primary CMB anisotropies remain consistent with GR at recombination, as T(a) → 0 implies an effectively null EFC modification at z ∼ 1100.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Next-generation CMB (e.g., Simons Observatory, CMB-S4) detecting a statistically significant early-time deviation consistent with an EFC-like background coupling at recombination.

sealed_predictions.statement: BAO+RSD datasets that probe z ∼ 0.4–0.7 mildly prefer β > 0 with suppressed growth relative to ΛCDM (directional test consistent with BOSS DR12).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: DESI/Euclid BAO+RSD combined likelihoods showing no improvement (or a negative preference) for β > 0 and/or favouring β ≤ 0.

sealed_predictions.statement: SN Ia Hubble-diagram residuals shift slightly negative, with |Δμ| ≤ 0.032 mag over 0.1 ≤ z ≤ 1, consistent with mildly smaller distances from the modified H(a).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision SN Ia samples (e.g., Pantheon++/Roman) measuring a residual pattern inconsistent in sign or amplitude with the predicted modest negative Δμ.

kill_criteria: KC1: DESI/Euclid BAO+RSD jointly prefer no improvement for β>0 (e.g., Δχ2 ≥ 0 relative to ΛCDM) and/or yield a best-fit β ≤ 0 with >2σ significance.
KC2: Robust (>3σ) detection of a non-null EFC background imprint in Lyα P1D at z ≈ 3, contradicting the predicted strong suppression (practical null) at high redshift.
KC3: Statistically significant evidence for early-time (recombination-era) deviations attributable to EFC background coupling, contradicting the GR-recovery envelope implied by T(a) → 0 at z ∼ 1100.

KC4: RSD measurements at z ∼ 0.4–0.7 favour growth enhancement (Poisson-channel μ>1) over growth suppression with a >3σ preference, reversing the direction required by the EFC background-coupling test.

falsification_criteria.observation: Large μ − 1 at z > 2 where Ωₘ ≈ 1
Poisson μ > 1 detected at α_L2 level

key_conclusions: Poisson-equation coupling (μ > 1) is excluded by BOSS RSD
EFC enters through the Friedmann equation, not Poisson
β = 0.08 shows mild preference in combined BAO + RSD (Δχ² = −3.89, ~2σ)
Independently consistent with CMB lensing and SN Ia
Four channels, one parameter, zero kills
Regime passes at z = 3 and z = 1100 are automatic consequences of T(a) → 0
architectural_constraint: EFC behaves as a dynamical dark-energy-like background effect, not as classical modified gravity in the Poisson term
